title: Session handoff experiments — hosted to private prototype
content:
Quick purpose: sketching a minimal prototype to test user-visible session handoff when a customer moves an ongoing user conversation from hosted API -> their Private deployment (VPC or on-prem).

Why this matters (short): customers ask for migration/playback, SREs want predictable routing, and product wants a clear UX for continuity (no abrupt resets). Current assumptions: we persist KV cache and conversation history on hosted metadata store; private deployments have separate stores. Handoff needs: identity mapping, secure transfer of session state, compatibility of model/quantization, and routing policies.

High-level goals:
- Operator goal: enable seamless in-flight session transfer with <200ms extra latency for first post-handoff request.
- User goal: no visible loss of context in next 3 messages after handoff.
- Platform goal: maintain security (customer-owned keys or tokenized transfer) and clear audit trail.

User stories (lean):
- As an SRE, I can trigger a session export for a given session_id and target deployment so that the user continues on private infra.
- As an engineer on a customer app, I want the session to remain coherent after migrating to a private cluster so users don't re-send context.
- As a product manager, I want a fallback route so if private capacity isn't ready, requests continue against hosted model variants automatically.

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- End-to-end session move completes within 5s for 95% of sessions in test harness (includes transfer + validation).
- Post-handoff first-turn answer has embedding/semantic similarity >= 0.9 to baseline (same prompt + pre-handoff KV).
- Audit log created with transfer id, origin, target, timestamp, and operator id.

Technical approaches (brainstormed options):
1) Controlled export/import (preferred for prototype):
   - Export: serialize KV cache (keys + optional prefix cache), conversation slab (last N messages), model_id + quantization metadata, and signed checksum.
   - Transfer: upload to customer-owned S3 or pre-provisioned bucket; use short-lived signed URL; issue linear ticket for encryption keys if needed.
   - Import: target runtime validates checksum and model compatibility; warms KV into long-lived KV store; marks session as owned by target routing policy.
   - Pros: simple, clear audit trail. Cons: data movement costs, relies on bucket access.

2) Streaming handshake via control plane:
   - Keep data in-hosted for short TTL; control-plane coordinates live redirect and ephemeral session token exchange.
   - Pros: minimum copy, good for quick handoffs. Cons: control-plane becomes critical path, cross-region concerns.

3) Hybrid delta sync:
   - Transfer only diffs (recent tokens + embeddings) and rely on canonical transcript in customer storage.
   - Might be useful for very large sessions.

Security considerations (must-check):
- Ensure transfer respects customer data residency (region tag).
- Offer two modes: customer-managed bucket (preferred) or Redwood-encrypted staging with automatic purge.
- Key/credential flow: support KMS-wrapped signing or ephemeral tokens with least privilege.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 0 (lab): local dev runtime + two containers (hosted-sim, private-sim). Implement option 1 export/import with small sessions.
- Phase 1 (internal beta): run 1000 synthetic sessions, measure integrity (similarity + turn continuity) and latency.
- Phase 2 (customer pilot): pilot with 1-2 internal-friendly customers on staging private deployment. Collect UX notes.

Metrics to track:
- transfer_duration_p50/p95
- first_post_handoff_latency
- semantic_similarity_first_response (embedding cosine with baseline)
- #failed_transfers and root cause tags (permission, model_mismatch, size_limit)
- rollback_rate when fallback triggered

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: how to handle model mismatches (model family vs exact checkpoint)? allowed downgrade rules? TODO: draft model compatibility matrix.
- Q: limit on session size (tokens + kv bytes). Propose default 2MB; investigate costs.
- TODO: mock UI text for console: "Move active session to Private cluster" + confirm modal + estimated transfer time.
- TODO: talk to infra about short-lived bucket patterns and cross-org ACLs (tag @noah).

Edge cases to consider:
- Active streaming request during transfer (race). Possible fix: quiesce new requests for session_id until move done or route to fallback.
- Partial transfer (network error) -> need atomicity / tombstone marker and retry logic.
- GDPR deletion requests mid-transfer -> flush and honor.

Rough rollout UX sketches (notes to self):
- Console: session table with "Transfer" action; modal shows estimated size + time + required permissions.
- API: POST /sessions/:id/move { target_deployment, transfer_mode: "s3"|"control_plane" } returns transfer_id. GET /transfers/:id status.
- Webhook: optional callback to customer on completion.

Possible quick experiments to validate feasibility without infra changes:
- Rehydrate by replay: in-hosted export -> import into a sandbox runtime that uses same model and measure similarity.
- Simulate large session cost by generating large KV and measuring serialization time.

Notes to self / meeting prep (for sync with Noah + Maya):
- Bring model compatibility sketch, cost estimate for S3 transfers, and 1-pager on security modes.
- Ask infra about quotas on ephemeral staging buckets and cross-account ACL patterns.
- Goal for sync: define MVP approach (I vote option 1) and surface any blocking infra constraints.

References / related tickets:
- Linear: PROD-412 (session-handoff design)
- GH: rti PR 1287 (session export helpers)
- Slack: #eng-inference thread starting 2025-09-24 (search "session handoff")

Final quick todo list (next week):
- [ ] prototype exporter (Azra)
- [ ] list of model compatibility rules (Maya)
- [ ] infra feasibility for staging bucket (Noah)
- [ ] mock console flow + copy (PM)

Rough thought: long-term this could be generalized as "session portability" (moves between regions, between Dedicated pools, and between hosted/private). For MVP keep scope: hosted -> private only.

-- end of notes (very rough)
